findings.title: FBI FLASH-20261113-001: Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework
findings.summary_md: The FBI issued FLASH-20261113-001, titled Threat Overview of ARTEX Autonomous Penetration Testing Framework, on 13 November 2026 and marked it TLP:CLEAR. The advisory highlights tactics, techniques and procedures and indicators of compromise associated with ARTEX, the autonomous penetration testing framework the FBI says multiple actors have abused since at least August 2026. It predates the first report of Barracuda as a victim by three days.

findings.title: ARTEX and Friends: Enter Agentic Offensive Frameworks
findings.summary_md: Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant reported on 30 October 2026 that multiple threat actors were abusing ARTEX, Hexstrike and CAIRN in incident response engagements. The post says ARTEX was released by developer Autumn-27, is written in Go with an embedded Next.js web console, and was taken down from GitHub in October 2026 while forks, localized variants such as ScopeWeaver and a commercial version called ARTEX PRO kept circulating. GTIG observed automated Active Directory reconnaissance, privilege escalation, Azure storage key harvesting and custom webshell deployment in activity dating to late August 2026.

findings.title: ARTEX: Attackers apply agentic AI
findings.summary_md: Sophos X-Ops published its ARTEX analysis on 10 November 2026, describing a Go-based multi-agent framework whose planning agents map targets and whose worker agents run scanning, exploitation, credential access and webshell deployment. The post names the mid-October ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise as a prominent case, which Microsoft attributes to China-state-aligned Storm-0940. Sophos notes that operators supplied ARTEX with authentication material or compromised application credentials for use against cloud APIs and services such as Microsoft Graph, and lists its own coverage for the observed behaviors.

findings.title: ARTEX and AI-Powered Red Teaming Tools: What Defenders Need to Know
findings.summary_md: Unit 42 published defensive guidance on 11 November 2026 after tracking ARTEX in intrusion attempts and a coordinated campaign against customer cloud environments in retail, consulting and other sectors. As of October 2026 it counted 609 internet-facing ARTEX hosts and 1,323 running CyberStrikeAI, with 21 running both, and documented a cadence of one to 14 requests about a second apart followed by pauses of 25 to 31 seconds. Recommendations include removing public OpenAPI specifications and source maps, requiring authentication on every write endpoint, replacing long-lived cloud keys, and hunting canary usernames, first use of a cloud key from a new IP and write-then-delete storage tests.

findings.title: Amazon Threat Intelligence observes threat actors running cybercrime campaigns with ARTEX AI agents
findings.summary_md: Amazon Threat Intelligence reported on 13 November 2026 that its MadPot decoy sensors captured, between 3 October and 5 November 2026, AI agent requests carrying operating memory from ARTEX campaigns. The records described a credential-theft operation that fed stolen AI model keys back into the framework to pay for further hunting, and a separate campaign against two cryptocurrency exchanges using real-time deepfake video and forged identity documents. AWS published IP indicators with first and last seen dates and advised treating AI applications, model gateways and inference endpoints as production systems while watching for unusual spend.

findings.title: ARTEX and beyond: AI-enabled penetration testing platforms
findings.summary_md: Cisco Talos published an advisory on 13 November 2026 on growing in-the-wild use of AI-enabled penetration testing frameworks, including ARTEX. It describes ARTEX as developed under the pseudonym Autumn-27 and released on GitHub in July 2026, with planner and worker agents and a shared graph of assets, findings and progress. Talos found ARTEX deployed alongside VShell, GoPhish and AdaptixC2 through its Model Context Protocol extensibility, and cited CrowdStrike attribution of an espionage campaign beginning 17 October 2026 to VAPOR PANDA using ARTEX against more than 200 organizations.
